newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Army sergeant guilty of 18 rape counts.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Army sergeant guilty of 18 rape counts.

text.p: A U.S. military jury on Tuesday found an army staff sergeant guilty of 18 counts of rape in the most prominent case in a major sexual misconduct scandal shaking the military.

U.S. Army Staff Sgt. Delmar Simpson was acquitted on one additional rape count but found guilty of indecent assault. He also was found guilty of 25 of 35 other sexual misconduct counts against him, not guilty of seven and guilty of lesser offences on three.

Simpson, 32, could face life in prison for the rape convictions. He already had pleaded guilty to 11 counts of consensual sex and five counts of propositioning, for which he faced a maximum sentence of 32 years in prison.

The six-member court-martial panel had deliberated for 31 hours over five days after a 10-day trial in the case, which involved six female trainees at the Aberdeen Proving Ground's Ordnance Centre and School.
Simpson's is the highest profile case in a major sexual misconduct investigation at the base, which has become the military's biggest sexual harassment scandal since the Navy's 1991 Tailhook affair.
After the verdicts, Army Trial Judge Col. Paul Johnston granted a defence motion to postpone the sentencing hearing and court recessed until Monday.
The Defence Department declined immediate comment on the conviction, noting the military's justice system provided for an extensive appeals process for Simpson.
"This proceeding is not over," Pentagon spokesman Ken Bacon told reporters in Washington.

"If the Army court of appeals upholds the verdict, then the individual can appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Armed Forces," Bacon said. If that court does not take the case, then Simpson could go to the U.S. Supreme Court.

Simpson was the first of 12 trainers charged with various acts of misconduct at Aberdeen to go before a court-martial and was charged with the most rapes. Four cases were settled earlier through plea agreements or administrative proceedings, although none had yielded a rape conviction.

Military trial expert Eugene Fidell called the sweeping slate of convictions "an impressive achievement for the prosecution" that should send a clear warning to the other 11 Aberdeen trainers to settle before a court-martial.
Lt. Col. Gabriel Riesco, chief of staff at Aberdeen's Ordnance Centre and School, said after the verdict that the military was hoping for a speedy conclusion to all the cases.

"I just want to emphasise that we are continuing with our quest to process all these cases expeditiously. We are interested in protecting the victims as much as possible and we also continue to investigate, to root out the systemic causes of all this," he said.
